references.text: Refers to the tribal chiefs of Edom (אַלּוּפֵי אֱדוֹם), mentioned in Moses' song
Moab was seized with fear and dread for the people of Israel, reflecting the reaction described in the song
Prophecy of Israel's victory over Edom and Moab, confirming the fear these nations had
Edom's fear of Israel is confirmed; they were afraid (יְרֵאִים) of the people of Israel
God placed fear and trembling (רַעַד) upon all peoples under heaven because of Israel
Rahab confirms that the inhabitants of Canaan melted away (נָמֹגוּ) with fear when they heard about the exodus from Egypt
The hearts of the Canaanites melted, and they lost courage when they heard of Israel's progress
Describes how trembling (רַעַד) seized the leaders when they saw God's power
Egypt will tremble with fear at the Lord's hand, a similar reaction to that of Edom, Moab, and Canaan
Canaan and Midian trembled with fear, a poetic echo of the peoples' fear during the exodus
Jeremiah 48:39 highlights the consequence of the fear experienced by Edom and Moab in Exodus, showing how this fear develops into complete shame and destruction.
Numbers 22:3 provides the historical context for Moab's enduring fear that began in Exodus 15.
